description:
should_gc counts on-heap young bytes only. A process that makes large binaries (over SHARED_BIN_THRESHOLD_BYTES = 64, runtime/src/heap/mod.rs:83) puts a 32-byte ProcBin stub on the heap and the bytes off-heap (Heap::alloc_bitstring, runtime/src/heap/imp.rs:855). The dead stubs, and so the off-heap bytes, are freed only at a collection, which those 32-byte stubs alone rarely trigger.
Measured on c5a03e198 and develop: String.duplicate("abcdefgh", 16000) makes 15,992 shared binaries totalling 1,024,063,712 bytes with zero fz.runtime.gc events and a 1.17 GB peak RSS (GC heap a few MB). Peak RSS 34 MB / 100 MB / 1117 MB at 8/32/128 KB of input. Repro: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/d1d265b3-f8e7-419b-8316-906f89c17e6b/scratchpad/9x7-gc/repro/binwalk.fz, dup.fz, bwstats.fz.
BEAM counts referenced off-heap binary bytes as virtual heap and collects when it overflows. Experiment first, with predictions: count live stub bytes into the trigger; measure peak RSS on the repro and the distiller and instructions on the suite. Interacts with fz-9x7.7 (minimum young size) and fz-sc8.208 (binary views).

The measurement above used the quadratic String.duplicate that develop replaced in PR #588 (a939d32e8), so most of those bytes were its intermediate results. The trigger gap still holds by construction, but the numbers must be re-measured on develop with a repro that makes dead large binaries directly, and again after fz-sc8.208 lands (about 560 -> 140 stubs per distiller line).

comments.text: Refuted after five pre-registered rounds (scratch 9x7-8/notes.md, results{,2,4,5}.txt, page https://claude.ai/artifact/QydSk1Cp2zZs8PiAqix8sp). Rounds 2-3: young binary bytes in the heap trigger (256 B floor) cut deadbinlive RSS 202->73 MB with every guard in range. Round 4: that variant regresses survive vs today (168->230 MB); old-binary majors (A) cost the distiller 4.0x RSS / 1.22x instructions; quantum cut (B) costs deadbin 2.14x instructions. Round 5 (OTP-shaped separate binary budgets, 256 KiB minimum, judged vs today, 147 runs/variant): F, O, F+C, O+C all fail rules 2 and 3 on dist-p28000 (RSS 1.74-1.77x), dist-full (RSS 3.98-4.35x, instr 1.20-1.27x), json (RSS 1.15-1.22x, instr 1.09-1.14x) and rule 2 on survive (instr 1.19-1.26x). The quantum cut at a 256 KiB minimum works: quantum 125 MB -> 0.3 MB off-heap at no instruction cost. Mechanism of the distiller regression is unverified; the only clause F, O and round-4 A share is the old-binary major.
Reopened (user approved page https://claude.ai/artifact/PC7vJ3veeQqqQca2ppEnWp): revisit as round 6 on the aged collector of fz-9x7.11; round 6 is pre-registered when fz-9x7.11 lands.

Round 6 (bench, arms built from exp/9x7-8-r6 535b3c9d2 on 8a2452976, 25 interleaved runs, dist-full 9; outputs identical on every workload). Pre-registered verdict: ALL ARMS FAIL. F: clause 1 fails (deadbinlive time-weighted in-use 0.780 of V0, rule needs <=0.75), clauses 2 and 3 pass. O: clause 1 fails; clause 2 fails on survive (i1.115), enum (i1.118), qsort (i1.034). FC/OC: clause 1 and 4 fail (quantum tw 1.264); OC also clause 2. F highlights: deadbinlive peak in-use 0.227 of V0 (119.9 -> 27.2 MB), cycles 0.736, instructions 0.937; giftbin under FC peak 0.131 and tw 0.193; survive peak 1.045 (inside clause 3's 5%). MEASUREMENT DEFECT found after the run: the time-weighted in-use figure is computed from gc events only, holding the last sample until the next collection. On survive V0 in-use reaches its 101.5 MB peak between collections at 12.9 ms and 36.6 ms while the estimator holds 17.4 MB for that span, so tw under-reports exactly the arms that collect less: survive's F tw 2.33x and deadbinlive's 0.78 are not trustworthy. Clauses 1 and 4 rest on that estimator; clause 3 (peak, exact) is sound. Unexplained: O costs +11.8% instructions on enum, which allocates no binaries and has the same gc count as F. Ticket stays open; the measurement fix is proposed to the user.

Round 6 RE-JUDGED with the exact allocation-weighted mean in-use (integral from refuted fz-9x7.29 compiled into the experiment arms only; arms rebuilt from exp/9x7-8-r6 + one probe commit; deterministic, measured locally). Clauses 1 and 4 now: deadbinlive mean F 0.302, O 0.302, FC 0.314, OC 0.314 of V0 (rule <=0.75: all pass); quantum mean FC 0.003, OC 0.003 (clause 4 <=0.75: pass). Clauses 2 and 3 stand from the bench round (F, FC pass; O, OC fail clause 2). VERDICT: F PASSES, FC PASSES, O and OC FAIL. Choice rule 'F over O; C only if it passes' selects FC. Prediction 'FC/OC fail on survive' was wrong. Not covered by any clause and reported: survive's mean in-use rises 13.5% under F and FC (40.6 MB -> 46.0 MB) while its peak stays within clause 3 (1.025-1.045). Other FC means: deadbin 0.136, giftbin 0.133, json 0.969, everything else 1.000. Next: production FC built clean (no spike code), stacked on the fz-9x7.25/.28 stack.

Production FC built clean: c0e637308 on fz-9x7.8/binary-trigger (on d5cbd823c; will restack after .28). Quantum cut at the allocation call site via Process::alloc_bitstring/_with/alloc_concatenation (heap exposes binary_budget.is_due(); offset_of! shim gone); message copies count toward the receiver's budget but cut no quantum. A/B vs d5cbd823c, 5 runs: outputs identical on 16 workloads; instructions quantum 0.92, deadbinlive 0.91, ring 1.010, survive 1.005, dist 1.002, others 0.99-1.00. peak_in_use: deadbinlive 0.244, quantum 0.020, deadbin 0.58, giftbin 0.53 (base peaks ~5 MB; runtime floor ~1.6 MB), survive 1.025, json 0.997. gc counts match the round-6 FC spike exactly (survive 41, quantum 5000, deadbin 390, deadbinlive 418, giftbin 780, json 46). No pin changed. Full gate green (6952 passed).

FC cost attribution (user-approved experiments; data in scratchpad/8probe/). (1) survive: pre-registered hypothesis 'majors free more dead binaries under FC' REFUTED (major-freed binary bytes base 79.4 MB vs FC 30.3 MB). Actual mechanism: FC's extra minors promote binary-owning list cells; dead old-owned binaries are freed only by a major; the major trigger counts only old HEAP bytes (~5-6 MB, never grows enough), so after FC's last major at 16.7 ms (run ~60 ms) 7 more minors run and no major: binary_in_use climbs to 48 MB vs ~10 MB live (base peak 15 MB; base's one late major freed 79 MB). Binary part = ~73% of the time-weighted post-gc in_use gap; rest heap blocks. (2) ring on bench, 9 interleaved runs: FC 0.9885x instructions (spread 0.87%/0.23%), msg 0.9821x, spin 0.9999x; local +1.0% did not reproduce; gc counts and event streams identical -> codegen/layout, no extra work. Proposal: the major trigger also counts old-held binary bytes (major due when held binary bytes outgrow MAJOR_GROWTH_FACTOR x those left by the last major, as BEAM's old vheap does), folded into .8 before decision 43.

title: Off-heap binary bytes count toward the collection trigger
